answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create pressure, but the 94% line utilization removes safety margin for delivery risk. Memory_c2 shows switching to low-cost vendor cuts cost but introduces SLA miss risk—unacceptable here. Memory_c4 demonstrates renegotiation at renewal recovered margin and moved incumbent on both price and terms. Memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing without scope cuts. Verification of c2 and c4 will clarify the realistic cost recovery range and incumbent flexibility. Negotiating terms—leveraging the renewal moment to demand both price reduction (targeting ~12-15% from the 18% goal) and locked multi-year volume pricing (per c6)—balances the cost mandate against delivery stability. This preserves the incumbent's proven integration (c1) while extracting real concessions. If negotiation yields insufficient savings, a second-source strategy becomes viable in the next cycle without rushing a risky sole-source switch. The single sourcing decision slot is deployed where it unlocks immediate margin recovery and preserves options.
